description: Read endpoint GET /api/v1/heartbeats/{id}/history mirroring monitor history, its OpenAPI contract, and the no-MCP-change confirmation. Depends on FEAT-001 (the Timescale store methods QueryHeartbeatEvents/CountHeartbeatEventsByType and the heartbeats.history_retention_days column/response). Returns discrete events plus a summary (uptime %, missed/fail/success counts). step is accepted and validated for symmetry with monitor history but is inert in v1.
steps: Create backend/internal/api/handlers/heartbeat_history.go with type HeartbeatHistoryHandler{ queries *db.Queries; tsStore *timescale.Store }, NewHeartbeatHistoryHandler(queries, tsStore), and Register(rg *gin.RouterGroup) mounting rg.GET("/heartbeats/:id/history", h.GetHistory). GetHistory mirrors history.go: parse optional step and validate [60,86400] -> 400 INVALID_STEP (echoed back but inert, no server-side bucketing); parse id as UUID -> 400 INVALID_ID; GetHeartbeat(id) -> 404 NOT_FOUND "heartbeat not found"; default window now-24h..now; parse from/to RFC3339 -> 400 VALIDATION_ERROR on bad value; require from.Before(to) else 400 VALIDATION_ERROR "from must be before to"; retentionClamp(from, now, hb.HistoryRetentionDays) for truncated.

Build the response per design section 4.3: top-level heartbeat_id, from, to (RFC3339), truncated; summary{ uptime_percent (float 1 decimal = success_count/total_events*100, JSON null when total_events==0), missed_count, fail_count, success_count, total_events }; events[] each { event_type, previous_state (omitempty), occurred_at RFC3339 }. Use QueryHeartbeatEvents for events (initialize make([]..., 0, n) so it serializes as [] never null) and CountHeartbeatEventsByType for the summary. Enforce the invariant success_count + fail_count + missed_count == total_events.

Register the handler in backend/internal/api/router.go inside the protected group, gated by `if deps.TimescaleStore != nil`, immediately after the heartbeat CRUD handler registration: historyHandler := handlers.NewHeartbeatHistoryHandler(deps.Queries, deps.TimescaleStore); historyHandler.Register(protected).

Add unit tests in backend/internal/api/handlers/heartbeat_history_test.go: from/to defaults, invalid timestamps, from>=to, invalid step, bad UUID, retention clamping; summary math (uptime_percent = success_count/total_events*100, null at zero events, invariant success+fail+missed == total, and that both fail and missed reduce uptime equally).

Update backend/api/openapi.yaml in THIS change: add path GET /heartbeats/{id}/history under the heartbeats tag with the id path param, from/to/step query params, a 200 referencing a new HeartbeatHistoryResponse schema, and 400/404 referencing the existing error envelope. Add schemas HeartbeatHistoryResponse, HeartbeatEvent (event_type enum [success,fail,missed]; previous_state enum [up,down,paused,new]), and HeartbeatHistorySummary matching the response exactly. Add history_retention_days (integer, minimum 1, maximum 365, default 30) to the existing heartbeat request and response schemas, mirroring the monitor schema.

Confirm no MCP change is needed: grep mcp/internal/ for any consumer of /heartbeats and confirm the route is absent from the AGENTS.md MCP co-change list; record the result (expected: no MCP changes) in the FEAT findings.
acceptance_criteria: `cd backend && go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/pulse` succeeds with the new handler registered.
`cd backend && go test -race -count=1 ./...` passes, including the new heartbeat_history handler tests (param parsing, retention clamp, summary math + invariant).

GET /api/v1/heartbeats/{id}/history returns the design-section-4.3 shape: 400 INVALID_ID / INVALID_STEP / VALIDATION_ERROR and 404 NOT_FOUND as specified; events is [] (never null) when empty; summary.uptime_percent is null when total_events==0.
backend/api/openapi.yaml documents the new path and schemas and the history_retention_days property in the same change; the enums match the handler.
A grep of mcp/internal/ confirms no heartbeat consumer, so no MCP change is made; the determination is recorded in findings.
verification: grep -rn "heartbeat" mcp/internal/ || true  (expect no tool/client consumer; document the output)

findings:
FEAT-002 complete. Read endpoint + OpenAPI + no-MCP confirmation shipped.

ENDPOINT (for FEAT-003 frontend): GET /api/v1/heartbeats/{id}/history. Registered in backend/internal/api/router.go inside the protected group (JWT or Bearer API token), gated on `if deps.TimescaleStore != nil`, immediately after heartbeatHandler.Register(protected). Query params: from, to (RFC3339, default now-24h..now), step (int, validated [60,86400] -> 400 INVALID_STEP, but INERT in v1 — echoed-validated only, no bucketing, not even returned in the response). step is validated BEFORE the id UUID parse.

RESPONSE SHAPE (handler type heartbeatHistoryResponse in backend/internal/api/handlers/heartbeat_history.go) — exact JSON field names + nullability for FEAT-003 TS types:
- heartbeat_id: string (uuid)
- from: string (RFC3339, EFFECTIVE start after retention clamp)
- to: string (RFC3339)
- truncated: bool (true when from was clamped to now - history_retention_days)
- summary: object {
    uptime_percent: number|null  (NOT omitempty — serialized as JSON null when total_events==0; else success_count/total_events*100 rounded to 1 decimal, range 0..100),
    missed_count: number (int64),
    fail_count: number (int64),
    success_count: number (int64),
    total_events: number (int64)
  }
- events: array (ALWAYS present, [] never null — make([]..,0,n)) of {
    event_type: 'success'|'fail'|'missed',
    previous_state?: 'up'|'down'|'paused'|'new'  (omitempty — OMITTED from JSON when null, so optional in TS),
    occurred_at: string (RFC3339)
  }. events are ascending by occurred_at (chronological, left->right on the timeline).

INVARIANT: success_count + fail_count + missed_count == total_events (total is computed as that sum). Both fail and missed reduce uptime equally; only success counts as up.

ERROR CODES (standard envelope {error:{code,message}}, X-Request-ID header always set): 400 INVALID_STEP (step out of [60,86400] or non-int); 400 INVALID_ID (bad UUID); 404 NOT_FOUND ('heartbeat not found'); 400 VALIDATION_ERROR (bad from/to RFC3339, or from not strictly before to -> 'from must be before to'); 500 DB_ERROR (store failure). Empty window / brand-new heartbeat => 200 with events:[], summary.uptime_percent:null, all counts 0 (NOT an error) — FEAT-003 must render an explicit empty state (there is no backfill).

STORE USAGE: handler calls deps.TimescaleStore.QueryHeartbeatEvents(ctx,id,from,to) for events and CountHeartbeatEventsByType(ctx,id,from,to) for the summary (two bounded queries over the clamped window, no N+1). Retention clamp reuses the existing retentionClamp(from, now, hb.HistoryRetentionDays) helper from history.go.

OPENAPI: backend/api/openapi.yaml already carried the path GET /heartbeats/{id}/history (operationId getHeartbeatHistory, Heartbeats tag, from/to/step params, 200 -> HeartbeatHistoryResponse, 400/404/401) and the schemas HeartbeatEvent, HeartbeatHistorySummary, HeartbeatHistoryResponse, plus history_retention_days (int 1..365 default 30) on both the Heartbeat response schema and CreateHeartbeatRequest. The only spec edit this feature made was adding the enum [up,down,paused,new] to HeartbeatEvent.previous_state to match design section 4.5 (it previously had nullable:true with no enum). event_type enum is [success,fail,missed]. All match the handler.

MCP: grep -rni 'heartbeat' mcp/internal/ returned NO matches (NO_MCP_HEARTBEAT_CONSUMER). The route is absent from the AGENTS.md MCP co-change list (which covers only monitor/incident/tag/dashboard endpoints). Determination: NO MCP change required.

TESTS: backend/internal/api/handlers/heartbeat_history_test.go (external, package handlers_test) covers INVALID_ID, INVALID_STEP (abc/59/86401/0/-1), NOT_FOUND, bad from, bad to, from==to, from>to — all via the shared heartbeatFakeDB with a nil *timescale.Store (those branches return before the store is touched). backend/internal/api/handlers/heartbeat_history_internal_test.go (in-package) covers the pure helpers: retentionClamp (within-retention unchanged; before-boundary clamped+truncated) and buildHeartbeatSummary (null uptime at zero events; 142/1/2 -> 97.9 and invariant; fail vs missed reduce uptime equally -> 80.0; all-success 100.0; no-success 0.0 not null). The store-backed happy path is covered by FEAT-001's DB-gated timescale round-trip tests.

VERIFICATION RESULTS: `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/pulse` OK. `go test -race -count=1 ./...` passes (all packages). `grep -rni heartbeat mcp/internal/` empty.
